what: From when the panel’s bottom edge touches the 90% line of the screen until it leaves the top, the panel sags down by .4 of the screen height and darkens to brightness .5 (no curve, scrub) — the next panel covers it from above so the previous one seems to sink back. Only at widths of 768px and up.

options.y: Sag distance (ratio of screen height), default .4
options.min: Applies only at this width (px) or wider, default 768 — 0 means always on

from.where: index reasons section·FAQ, works case section, dark panel below service·price (.js-c-remain)

index.js overlapping rising panel (.jt-overlap — original OverlapCard: from when the panel’s bottom edge passes 40% from the top of the screen until it leaves above the screen, the inside moves down 8rem with a black shade of .8, scrub 1.2)
from.options: y: 0.089; dim: 0.2; start: bottom 40%; end: bottom top; min: 0 — the original covers with a black veil (.8) instead of brightness, and the sag is 8rem (80px at 1440) rather than a screen ratio

note: Pre-applying will-change (transform, filter) to a big panel makes panels thousands of px tall exceed the compositing layer limit, and they render black on headless or low-end GPUs. Do not apply it.
